headline: Indiana, Florida and Alabama carried out executions on Thursday

paragraphs.text: Three states carried out the death penalty on Thursday, marking the second time in 2026 that three executions were carried out on the same day.

Jeffrey Weisheit, convicted of killing two children in a house fire, was pronounced dead in Indiana at 12:45 a.m. Gov. Mike Braun (R) had denied his lawyers’ request to change the sentence to life in prison.
Jesse Guardado, who had pleaded guilty to a fatal stabbing, was executed in Florida at 6:13 p.m. In his final statement, he apologized to the victim’s family, the AP reported.
Michael Taylor, who killed an elderly couple when he was 19, was executed an hour later in Alabama. Death penalty opponents had called for his sentence to be commuted given his young age at the time.
Alabama Gov. Kay Ivey (R) criticized Newsom’s decision in a statement to the AP, saying: “California may let their criminals escape justice, but not Alabama.”
The death penalty remains a divisive issue nationally, and executions have come under renewed scrutiny following Tennessee’s botched attempt to execute Christa Pike in September.
